Subject: KMS domain model & operator custody review (VPC/on-prem)

Hi team,

Attaching the first-pass proposal for the trust-domain separation we discussed for the FinServCo private deployment. High-level goals: isolate customer key material, minimize operator blast radius, and preserve ability to perform emergency unseal/rotation with full auditability.

Key points in the attachment and diagram:
- Three logical trust domains: Customer KEKs (BYOK HSMs), Redwood control plane wrap keys, and ephemeral runtime wrapping keys per-cluster.
- Operator roles strictly scoped: Operator-ReadOnly (monitoring), Operator-Wrap (wrap/unwrap tokens via ephemeral gateway), and Operator-Custody (physical handoff for hardware modules).
- Physical custody: when HSMs are on-prem, require dual sign-off and split custody envelopes for transport; for VPC-hosted HSMs we rely on vendor attestation + restricted KMS admin role.
- Rotation windows: propose staggered monthly rotations per trust domain; emergency rotation playbook attached as an appendix.

Questions for review:
1) Are the separation boundaries sufficient for a bank regulated under GLBA and PCI-like requirements?
2) Acceptable SLAs for operator-triggered rotations (target 30–45 minutes to rewrap runtime keys)?
3) Any objections to using Thales/HSM modules in split-custody on-prem flows?

Attachments: kms-trust-diagram-v1.png, operator-access-rules.pdf

Next steps: propose a 60-min design review Weds 10/28 to lock operator runbooks and audit hooks. Please flag anything that will block procurement/legal.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Infra Security

Karthik,

Thanks for the clear diagram. A few clarifications from our side before the review:
- For on-prem HSMs, what level of physical-proof will Redwood require when taking custody? We need a checklist for internal compliance and for our security team to sign off.
- Is there an option to run an HSM-in-place model where FinServCo keeps full possession and Redwood only gets wrapped keys (no hardware custody)?
- Rotation SLA: our ops wants to know the worst-case failover/rotation time if an operator-initiated wrap fails.

Also copied our procurement lead (procurement@finservco.com) to understand any contract-side constraints for split-custody logistics.

— FinServCo Infra

Hi everyone,

Thanks for the questions, FinServCo — replying inline to keep things concrete.

1) Physical-proof checklist (we'll add to the runbook):
   - Two-person witness sign-off on transport manifest (name + badge ID + timestamp).
   - Tamper-evident seals recorded on video; HSM serial verified pre/post move.
   - Chain-of-custody form (digital, signed) uploaded to the shared Drive folder.

2) HSM-in-place model:
   - Yes. We support BYOK where the customer retains HSM possession; in that mode Redwood never touches unwrapped customer KEKs. Integration: customer provides a wrapping public key or a secure endpoint that performs rewrap on their side. We lose ability to perform emergency unseal without customer participation, so that must be reflected in SLA and runbook.

3) Rotation SLA & failure modes:
   - Nominal: 5–15 minutes for runtime rewrap when automated (ephemeral wrapping key present).
   - Stagger edge-case (operator-assisted): 30–90 minutes depending on remote operator availability and network latency to on-prem HSM.
   - Worst-case (physical recovery + manual split-custody): hours to days — depends on shipping and customs for some regions.

Mitigations we propose:
- Maintain an escrow-wrapped KEK under strict legal control (multi-sig escrow) for catastrophic recovery; use only with documented approval chain and audited access.
- Ephemeral wrapping key per cluster with short TTLs to limit exposure.
- Audit hooks: every wrap/unwrap action emits a signed event to the control plane and to customer's audit endpoint (webhook + S3 archival).

I've attached an initial rotation schedule (rotation-schedule-v2.csv) that staggers customer KEK rotations so we avoid correlated restarts across regional clusters.

— Mina

> I've attached an initial rotation schedule (rotation-schedule-v2.csv) that staggers customer KEK rotations so we avoid correlated restarts across regional clusters.

Agree with Mina's mitigations. A couple of additions from an ops/runbook perspective:
- Add an "Emergency Rollback Playbook" section that describes how to quickly switch to read-only mode and fail traffic to a compatible model variant if a rewrap fails mid-commit. Keep runbook sub-steps minimal and scriptable.
- Operator authentication: require hardware-backed MFA for Operator-Wrap and Operator-Custody roles; do not allow API key-only access for any wrap/unwrap operations.
- Test cadence: quarterly dry-run of failover/rotation with FinServCo (tabletop plus 1 live simulated rewrap) to validate timing and roles.

I can draft the playbook appendix and coordinate the tabletop run with FinServCo ops if they agree.

— Soojin
